title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 61 (Power of Limited Company to Alter Its Share Capital)

content.overview: Section 61 allows a limited company having a share capital, if so authorised by its articles, to alter its memorandum to increase authorised capital; consolidate and divide shares; convert fully paid shares into stock and reconvert; sub-divide shares; or cancel unissued shares. Certain alterations (e.g. consolidation or division that results in a change in voting percentage of shareholders) require Tribunal approval. Cancellation of unissued shares does not amount to a reduction of share capital under the Act.
content.glance: Articles-authorised alteration of capital: increase; consolidate/divide; convert to/from stock; sub-divide; cancel unissued; Tribunal approval where voting percentage changes; cancel ≠ reduction.
content.study: A limited company having a share capital may, if so authorised by its articles, alter its memorandum in its general meeting to: increase its authorised share capital by such amount as it thinks expedient; consolidate and divide all or any of its share capital into shares of a larger amount than its existing shares; convert all or any of its fully paid-up shares into stock, and reconvert that stock into fully paid-up shares of any denomination; sub-divide its shares into shares of smaller amount than is fixed by the memorandum; or cancel shares which have not been taken or agreed to be taken and diminish the amount of its share capital by the amount of the shares so cancelled. Where consolidation or division results in a change in the voting percentage of shareholders, the alteration requires approval of the Tribunal. Cancellation under this section does not amount to a reduction of share capital within the meaning of the Act. Current-law framing: check articles authority; identify type of alteration; test Tribunal approval if voting percentage changes; note cancel ≠ reduction.

sections.heading: Authorised Alterations
sections.body: Increase authorised capital; consolidate and divide; convert fully paid shares into stock and reconvert; sub-divide; cancel unissued shares — if articles authorise.

sections.heading: Tribunal Approval
sections.body: Consolidation or division that changes the voting percentage of shareholders requires Tribunal approval.

sections.heading: Cancel Not Reduction
sections.body: Cancellation of unissued shares under s. 61 does not amount to a reduction of share capital under the Act.

examples.title: Increase of authorised capital
examples.body: Articles authorise. The company in general meeting increases authorised capital. Section 61 is applied; no Tribunal approval needed for a pure increase.

examples.title: Consolidation affecting voting
examples.body: Consolidation of shares would change voting percentages of shareholders. Tribunal approval is required under s. 61.

hypotheticals.question: Does cancelling unissued shares under s. 61 require the reduction procedure?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 61 expressly provides that such cancellation does not amount to a reduction of share capital under the Act.

misconceptions.trap: Any capital change under s. 61 needs Tribunal approval.
misconceptions.correction: Tribunal approval is required only where consolidation or division results in a change in voting percentage of shareholders.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 61 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Check articles. II. Identify type of alteration. III. Test voting-percentage change for Tribunal. IV. Note cancel ≠ reduction. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Articles; resolution; type of alteration; voting impact if any; precise relief.
